name: Example: Computing a "Less Than" Probability With the Exponential Distribution
problem: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(1\right),$ calculate $P\left(X < 2\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128540/assets/11a236eab01f3cf5c9a4af33a4f233d2ea9a98e4f244fa467adfdc27f7bba6b4.svg)

We're given that

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( 1 \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14128540/assets/e84b664ebb290db9007efb0d36ce7b9ce39f7da40763c8bbfc729b8bd347a646.svg)

Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(X < 2\right)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-x}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.8647\end{aligned}
$$
